title: Conrad Biermann's copybook of letters to Danish envoys abroad, Copenhagen 1675 (Rigsarkivet TKUA S-1418)

documents.shelfmark: Rigsarkivet, TKUA Almindelig del, Conrad Biermanns kopibog 1675 (S-1418), pp. [103]-105, Arkivalieronline images 108-109
documents.route: Copenhagen -> Paris (Biermann for the King to Meyercron)

plaintext.source: No decipherment in the copybook; the key sheet is in the TKUA 'Chiffer' 1670-1709 volume, image 55.

transcription.notes: The hook sign is written alike for set1 T (q), set2 A (g) and the number 9 (R); each instance labelled by stroke and checked by context.

system.summary: Each letter has two graphic signs and one number 1-24; names 25-276; an alphabetical code from 279 with open syllables in blocks and words between them.
system.notes: distinct_symbols counted in document A only. Other letters in the copybook use other keys (Spain, early Paris), not yet matched.

prior_solution.where: unknown After the key was found here (26 Oct 2026), Brice Dudout published readings of the image-55 letters to Høeg (eighteen letters, 2 Jan-5 June 1675) and Meyercrone (nineteen, 16 Feb-21 June; 6,103 groups, 99.4%) on Europe chiffrée, 27 Oct 2026, made independently.

conditions.human_role: Pasted the catalogue task; no other input.

solution.what: Web search for Biermann 1675 cipher, Danish diplomatic ciphers, TKUA Chiffer; nothing printed or online.
Copybook (255 images) and TKUA 'Chiffer' 1670-1709 (309 images) downloaded from the Rigsarkivet image API.
Key volume surveyed by contact sheets; images 1-52, 11 and 77 ruled out (later keys); image 55 (Pomponne 111 / Terlon 112) matched by its syllable values on the first cipher line.
Letter of 23 March 1675 to Meyercron deciphered with the image-55 key: 262/263 tokens give sense.
Image-55 key tried on the 2 January 1675 letter to Meyercron (image 4) and the letter to George Reetz in Spain (image 108 left): numbers do not fit; other keys.
Whole copybook surveyed page by page (survey_A/B.tsv): ~200 letters 2 Jan-24 June 1675, cipher on ~356 page sides; correspondents grouped by number ranges.
Image-55 key tried on Höegk 2 Jan (image 5): reads 'assez indulgent pour prendre la chose sur le mesme pied'; the key covers the Hague family.

All 309 key-volume images dated and 1670s keys (114-116, 145-147, 265, 294/295, 305-308 and others) tested on 10-20-token runs of the Lilienkron, Moscow, Spain, Sweden, Klingenberg, Lincker and early Paris letters; none reads. Image 94/95 fits 9/22 Klingenberg numbers but leaves 13 on blank slots.
Web searches for printed Meyercron and Just Høeg despatches of 1675: none found.

Eleven Høeg letters (2 Jan-9 Feb, 3,216 cipher tokens) transcribed from the images and deciphered with the image-55 key; the sheet resolves 97.2%, context values (new_values.tsv) bring each letter to 98-100% sense.

Values missing from the sheet inferred from repeated use: letter homophones among low numbers (26 n, 31 s, 33 u), names (279 Suédois, 67 l'Empereur, 582 Prince), syllables in the alphabetical gaps (598 que, 702 xe, 710 zo), and the open-square sign = l.

Brice Dudout's readings published (https://bdudout.github.io/europe-chiffree/en/documents.html#hoeg-1675, #meyercrone-1675): the image-55 key (his K55) reads the Høeg and Meyercrone letters of Jan-June 1675; the 2 Jan Meyercrone letter is in another key, as the survey here found. Scope here narrowed to Gioë, Schröder and the letters without a key.

outcome.method: read after matching with key from external sources
outcome.method_basis: The key sheet (TKUA 'Chiffer' 1670-1709, image 55) is filed in a separate key volume and had not been connected with the copybook; it reads document A.
outcome.fraction_read_source: reading_1675-03-23_meyercron.md, cipher tokens of document A only (the other letters of the copybook are not yet transcribed)

gaps.item: letters under the image-55 key (Høeg, Gioë in England, Schröder, Meyercron from late January)
letters without a surviving key (Lilienkron, Gioë Moscow, Reetz, Lindenow, Klingenberg, Lincker, Meyercron 2 Jan, Høeg 21 June, Lente 21 June)
document A p105.24: one open-square sign

outcome.notes: In progress: only one letter of the copybook read so far.

texts.summary: [You may send the Spanish ratification by the ordinary post,] which is still thought safe enough for that. The Swedish ambassador is not content with talking to others about the design his master the King has for our ‹543›: he has even spoken of it to Griffenfeld in a conversation the day before yesterday.

texts.label: Copenhagen to Just Høeg (The Hague), 15 May 1675 (img 184 · p. 180), Brice Dudout
texts.summary: You will see from what I am writing by this post to Mr de Klingenberg that His Majesty is thinking of sending you to the Elector of Brandenburg to stay with him for some time. It is not yet fully decided; once it is, you will be sent the credentials and instructions needed for this post.

texts.label: Copenhagen to Just Høeg (The Hague), 5 June 1675 (img 216 · pp. 211v–212), Brice Dudout
texts.summary: [I refer you to my letter to Mr de Klingenberg,] particularly on the Swedish ambassador’s suit for our princess. It was foreseen long ago that it would come to that.

texts.label: Copenhagen to Henning Meyercrone (Paris), 16 February 1675 (img 061 · p. 56v), Brice Dudout
texts.summary: [Pending new orders,] you need only continue with the method you have begun. His Majesty is well satisfied with all you said and answered to Pomponne, and wishes you to keep acting on that footing in the rest of your negotiation, in line with what your instructions set out more fully.

texts.label: Copenhagen to Henning Meyercrone (Paris), 23 February 1675 (img 067 · p. 62v), Brice Dudout
texts.summary: Mr de Terlon has again received letters from Mr de Pomponne detailing your second conversation with him, and saying that he is now seeking with you some compromise to remove the difficulty you made about agreeing to any signature at all.

texts.label: Copenhagen to Henning Meyercrone (Paris), 6 March 1675 (img 083–084 · pp. 79–79v), Brice Dudout
texts.summary: Some articles for an alliance with France are now being drawn up; they will be given to Terlon to learn his opinion.

texts.label: Copenhagen to Henning Meyercrone (Paris), 16 March 1675 (img 099 · p. 94v), Brice Dudout
texts.summary: France must not doubt that His Majesty will do, in this juncture, everything his honour can allow in favour of the King [Louis XIV]; Terlon received all the assurances he could wish this very morning, when he came to the castle to tell His Majesty how pleased the King his master had been with your audience.

texts.label: Copenhagen to Henning Meyercrone (Paris), 23 March 1675 (img 109 · pp. 104v–105), Brice Dudout

texts.label: Copenhagen to Henning Meyercrone (Paris), 30 March 1675 (img 114 · p. 110), Brice Dudout
texts.summary: [The Swedish ambassador] has had letters from Baron Sparre in France, writing that you complained with much exaggeration to Mr de Pomponne of the conditions Sweden is proposing to us, as unjust and even insulting to His Majesty. It seems to me that Pomponne might have handled what you told him a little more discreetly, since the matter speaks for itself.

texts.label: Copenhagen to Henning Meyercrone (Paris), 6 April 1675 (img 124–125 · pp. 120–120v), Brice Dudout
texts.summary: Spain and ‹163› (the province of Holland?) have paid their share of the money promised by the treaty concluded with His Majesty; but the other provinces are still behind, and the States are reluctant to break with Sweden themselves: you will see that things have hardly changed, and that you should therefore change nothing in your conduct where you are.

texts.summary: I wrote to you that a project would soon be given to Terlon, and Griffenfeld had it quite ready; but when it was debated in the council not all its members were of one mind, so it has not yet been handed over. texts.label: Copenhagen to Henning Meyercrone (Paris), 27 April 1675 (img 158–159 · pp. 154–154v), Brice Dudout
texts.summary: The King fully approves what you told Mr de Pomponne: the orders and instructions given to Høeg are entirely in keeping with it, as are the proposals he has made. You will have seen from my last why the project drawn up for Terlon has not yet been handed over, and Griffenfeld’s hope of overcoming the difficulties that delayed it.

texts.label: Copenhagen to Henning Meyercrone (Paris), 4 May 1675 (img 169 · p. 164v), Brice Dudout
texts.summary: The Grand Chancellor has also revised the project to be given to Mr de Terlon; you see that he neglects nothing to confirm France in the good feelings you have given her. He also spoke this afternoon to Mr von Stöcken to have you sent the money you need to follow the Most Christian King to the army.
